topicName: Distance and Probabilistic Models: KNeighborsClassifier and GaussianNB
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Distance and Probabilistic Models: KNeighborsClassifier and GaussianNB in Scikit-learn"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Supervised classification tasks in machine learning often rely on two fundamentally different paradigms: distance-based instance learning and probabilistic generative learning. In this tutorial, we will explore two classic algorithms implemented in Scikit-learn: KNeighborsClassifier and GaussianNB (Gaussian Naive Bayes)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Theoretical Foundations"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) is a non-parametric, lazy learning algorithm. It classifies a data point based on the majority vote of its k closest neighbors in the feature space, typically measured using Euclidean distance. Conversely, Gaussian Naive Bayes is a parametric, probabilistic classifier based on Bayes theorem, which assumes features are conditionally independent given the class label and follow a Gaussian (normal) distribution."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Setting Up the Environment and Dataset"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, we need to import the necessary modules from Scikit-learn, including datasets, preprocessing tools, metrics, and the two classifiers."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier
from sklearn.naive_bayes import GaussianNB
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, accuracy_score"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Next, we will load the classic Iris dataset, split it into training and testing sets, and scale the features. Feature scaling is particularly critical for distance-based models like KNN."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"iris = load_iris()
X, y = iris.data, iris.target

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)

scaler = StandardScaler()
X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Training and Evaluating KNeighborsClassifier"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"We initialize the KNeighborsClassifier with k=5 and fit the model using our scaled training data. Then, we generate predictions and evaluate the performance."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"knn = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=5, metric='euclidean')
knn.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)

y_pred_knn = knn.predict(X_test_scaled)
print('KNN Accuracy:', accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred_knn))"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Training and Evaluating GaussianNB"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Unlike KNN, Gaussian Naive Bayes does not strictly require feature scaling because it evaluates probability distributions per feature. We initialize and train GaussianNB on the unscaled training data."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"gnb = GaussianNB()
gnb.fit(X_train, y_train)

y_pred_gnb =gnb.predict(X_test)
print('GaussianNB Accuracy:', accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred_gnb))"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Comparing Model Outputs"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"To gain deeper insights, we can print out the full classification report for both models to inspect precision, recall, and f1-score."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"print('--- KNN Classification Report ---')
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred_knn, target_names=iris.target_names))

print('--- GaussianNB Classification Report ---')
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred_gnb, target_names=iris.target_names))"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Takeaways"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"KNeighborsClassifier relies on distance metrics, making feature scaling mandatory for optimal results."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"GaussianNB relies on probability distributions and Bayes theorem, assuming feature independence."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"KNN is a lazy learner (no explicit training phase, computations happen at query time), whereas GaussianNB is eager."}]
